vulnerability.title: Anonymous Azure Function Tester dumps runtime secrets
vulnerability.description: HTTP-triggered function Tester on a production Azure Function App (and its -dev- peer) was configured with authLevel:anonymous and no network restrictions. Unauthenticated GET returned the process environment as JSON, including Cosmos master key names, Storage account key material, MACHINEKEY_DecryptionKey, EasyAuth WEBSITE_AUTH_* keys, an AAD client secret, and an App Insights instrumentation key.
vulnerability.impact: Leaked Cosmos master key grants read/write/delete on an internet-accessible account backing identity and project records. Storage account key plus DataProtection key are prerequisites for code execution as the system-assigned managed identity (Key Vault secret get/set, Graph directory enum, ARM Owner on the app resource group). ACE was not demonstrated — production restart/code injection was out of ROE; prerequisites verified via ARM/Graph only.
vulnerability.evidence: Unauth GET /api/Tester returned JSON containing AzureWebJobsStorage, Cosmos ACCOUNT_ENDPOINT/key names, MACHINEKEY_DecryptionKey, WEBSITE_AUTH_ENCRYPTION_KEY, WEBSITE_AUTH_SIGNING_KEY, and App Insights key names. Values redacted.
vulnerability.remediation: Remove Tester or set authLevel=function and redeploy. Apply ipSecurityRestrictions or Private Endpoints. Determine if the app is still required; if not, decommission Function Apps, web apps, Cosmos, storage, Key Vaults, and AAD apps. Rotate Cosmos keys, storage keys, MACHINEKEY, WEBSITE_AUTH_*, App Insights, then AAD client secrets last after Tester is unreachable.
vulnerability.not_demonstrated: Arbitrary code execution as the Function App managed identity (would require writing a package and waiting for restart). Redeeming the live AAD client secret for Graph/ARM tokens. Item-level Cosmos dumps or destructive writes.
